column3: The Ammonites are called sons of Ammon; the son becoming king is expressed actively.
The Hebrew explicitly says they came to Hanun and repeats the purpose of comforting him.
The Hebrew mentions Hanun’s eyes and orders the purposes as exploring, overthrowing, and spying.
Beards are not explicitly named in this verse; the garments are cut halfway to the buttocks.
The reporting has a plural subject, and the beard is singular in Hebrew.
The battle front is pictured as its face.
The hand of Abishai is named; the verb of arraying for battle is plural.
The Hebrew repeats the stem for being strong without explicitly adding fighting.
The Hebrew calls it “the river” without explicitly naming the Euphrates.
The Hebrew repeats arraying for battle in a separate clause.
Hadadezer’s subjects are called servants, and they are said to serve David.
